correctness.rationale: The beta integral gives the scalar resolvent representations for exponents s and -s with 0<s<1, hence the matrix representations by spectral calculus. Sherman–Morrison factors (A+tI)^(-1)-(B+tI)^(-1) as tau/(1+tau u^T R_t u) times (R_t u)(R_t u)^T, where R_t=(A+tI)^(-1). Subtract the positive-power formulas using X(X+tI)^(-1)=I-t(X+tI)^(-1); subtract the negative-power ones in the opposite order. The two resulting weights are positive and proportional to t^s and t^(-s). Integrability follows from bounded R_t near zero and O(1/t) decay at infinity. Nonnegative continuous quadratic forms under the integrals vanish precisely when x^T R_t u vanishes for every t>0. Multiplying by the product of distinct denominators and evaluating at each negative eigenvalue then shows x orthogonal to each P_lambda u. Polynomial interpolation gives equality of their span with K(A,u), and spectral orthogonality gives exactly the stated active count even with repeated eigenvalues. Symmetry gives the common range and the endpoints s=1 give the rank-one forms directly. The square-root example checks by Cayley–Hamilton, (B+3I)^2=13B, and det(D)=5-18/sqrt(13)>0 since 325>324. The checker was inspected, not executed; its tolerance-based ranks are corroborative, not exact certificates for the theorem.
